title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 1] Problem Solving Techniques Using C Language (BCAGN1C01T)
- Unit I: Introduction to Programming & Algorithms
  * Computational problems, algorithm design concepts, top-down design approach, step-wise refinement.
  * Algorithm efficiency and correctness basics.
  * Structured programming principles: Sequence, Selection, Repetition.
  * Tools: Flowcharts, Pseudocode writing conventions.
- Unit II: Basics of C Programming Language
  * Data Representation: Fixed point, Floating point, 1's and 2's complement representation.
  * Tokens, Headers, Data types, Variables, Constants, Literals.
  * Operators: Arithmetic, Relational, Logical, Bitwise, Assignment, Increment/Decrement, Conditional.
  * Standard I/O operations: printf, scanf, formatted inputs/outputs.
  * Decision making: if, if-else, nested if-else, switch-case statements.
  * Loops: while, do-while, for loops.
- Unit III: Logic Development & Numerical Methods in C
  * Number manipulation: Digit extraction, reversal, prime checking, factorials, Fibonacci series, GCD/LCM, Armstrong numbers.
  * Base Conversions: Decimal to Binary/Octal/Hexadecimal and vice versa.
  * Taylor series approximations: Calculating pi, sin(x), cos(x), exponential series.
  * Jumps: break, continue, goto, exit statements.
- Unit IV: Arrays, Functions, Pointers & File Handling
  * Functions: Definition, Declaration, Function calls, Parameter passing (Call by Value vs Call by Reference), Scope and Lifetime of variables, Recursion.
  * Arrays: 1D arrays, 2D arrays (Matrix addition, subtraction, multiplication, transpose).
  * Strings: Character arrays, String manipulation functions (strlen, strcpy, strcat, strcmp), String sorting.
  * Pointers & Structures: Dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, free), Structures, Unions, File handling basics (fopen, fclose, fread, fwrite).
  * Searching & Sorting: Linear Search, Binary Search, Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 2] Computer Organization And Architecture (BCAGN1C02T)
- Unit I: Digital Logic & Codes
  * Boolean Algebra, Logic Gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR).
  * Simplification of Boolean Functions: Truth Tables, Canonical SOP/POS forms, Karnaugh Maps (2, 3, 4 variables).
  * Number Systems: Binary, Octal, Hexadecimal conversions.
  * Codes: Gray code, BCD, ASCII, EBCDIC.
- Unit II: Combinational & Sequential Circuits
  * Combinational Logic: Half Adder, Full Adder, Half Subtractor, Full Subtractor, Multiplexers (MUX), Demultiplexers (DEMUX), Decoders, Encoders.
  * Sequential Logic: Latches, Flip-Flops (SR, D, JK, T, Master-Slave).
  * Registers: Shift Registers, Universal Shift Registers, Counters (Synchronous, Asynchronous, Ring Counter).
- Unit III: Central Processing Unit (CPU) & Memory Hierarchy
  * Basic Computer Structure: Stored program concept, Instruction codes, Computer registers, Bus architecture.
  * Instruction Cycle: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Interrupt cycle.
  * CPU Architecture: General Register Organization, Stack Organization, Instruction formats (Zero, One, Two, Three address), Addressing Modes.
  * Architecture Types: RISC vs CISC features.
  * Memory Hierarchy: Cache Memory (Direct, Associative, Set-Associative Mapping), Main Memory (RAM/ROM), Virtual Memory, Secondary Storage.
- Unit IV: Input-Output Organization & Microprocessor
  * I/O Interfaces: Peripheral devices, Asynchronous data transfer, Strobe control, Handshaking.
  * Data Transfer Modes: Programmed I/O, Interrupt-initiated I/O, Direct Memory Access (DMA).
  * Microprocessor Architecture: Overview of Intel 8086 architecture, Pin configuration, Register set, Segment registers.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 3] Mathematical Foundation to Computer Science (BCAGN1E01T)
- Unit I: Set Theory, Relations & Functions
  * Set Theory: Sets, Subsets, Venn Diagrams, Set Operations, Power Sets, Cartesian Products.
  * Relations: Types of relations (Reflexive, Symmetric, Transitive, Equivalence), Partial Order Relations, Posets, Hasse Diagrams.
  * Closure of Relations: Warshall's Algorithm for Transitive Closure.
  * Functions: Injective (One-to-One), Surjective (Onto), Bijective, Inverse Functions, Function Composition.
  * Common Functions: Logarithmic, Exponential, Floor, Ceiling functions.
- Unit II: Combinatorics & Recurrence Relations
  * Counting Principles: Addition and Multiplication Rules, Pigeonhole Principle and Applications.
  * Permutations and Combinations, Binomial Theorem, Multinomial Theorem.
  * Recurrence Relations: Formulating recurrence relations, Solving linear homogeneous/non-homogeneous recurrence relations.
  * Generating Functions: Applications in solving recurrence (Tower of Hanoi, Fibonacci series).
- Unit III: Graph Theory & Trees
  * Graphs: Basic terminology, Directed & Undirected graphs, Degree of vertices, Handshaking Lemma, Subgraphs, Isomorphism.
  * Paths & Circuits: Eulerian Paths/Circuits, Hamiltonian Paths/Circuits.
  * Trees: Rooted Trees, Binary Trees, Spanning Trees, Minimum Spanning Trees (Prim's and Kruskal's Algorithms).
  * Special Graphs: Planar Graphs, Bipartite Graphs, Graph Coloring, Chromatic Number.
- Unit IV: Linear Algebra & Matrix Theory
  * Matrices: Matrix operations, Determinants, Inverse of a matrix using Adjoint and Elementary row operations.
  * Systems of Linear Equations: Consistency, Solution by Gaussian Elimination, Gauss-Jordan, Cramer's Rule.
  * Vector Spaces: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors, Characteristic Equation, Cayley-Hamilton Theorem.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 1] Operating System (BCAGN2C03T)
- Unit I: OS Architecture & System Structure
  * Definition, Objectives, Functions, Historical Evolution of OS (Batch, Multiprogramming, Time-sharing, Distributed, Real-time systems).
  * System Calls, System Programs, Operating System Services, System Structures (Monolithic, Layered, Microkernel, Modules).
  * Virtual Machines concepts.
- Unit II: Process Management & CPU Scheduling
  * Process Concept: Process Control Block (PCB), Process States, Process Transitions, Context Switching.
  * Threads: User-level threads vs Kernel-level threads, Multithreading Models.
  * CPU Scheduling: Schedulers (Long-term, Short-term, Medium-term), Preemptive vs Non-preemptive scheduling.
  * Scheduling Algorithms: FCFS, SJF (Shortest Job First), SRTF, Priority Scheduling, Round Robin, Multilevel Queue Scheduling.
- Unit III: Process Synchronization & Deadlocks
  * Inter-Process Communication (IPC): Shared Memory, Message Passing.
  * Critical Section Problem: Software Solutions (Peterson's Algorithm), Hardware Locks, Semaphores (Counting and Binary), Monitors.
  * Classical Synchronization Problems: Producer-Consumer, Readers-Writers, Dining Philosophers.
  * Deadlocks: System Model, Characterization (4 Necessary Conditions), Resource Allocation Graphs (RAG).
  * Deadlock Handling: Prevention, Avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), Detection, Recovery from Deadlock.
- Unit IV: Memory & Secondary Storage Management
  * Contiguous Memory Allocation: MVT, MFT, First-fit, Best-fit, Worst-fit, Fragmentation (Internal vs External).
  * Non-contiguous Allocation: Paging, Page Table Structure, Segmentation.
  * Virtual Memory: Demand Paging, Page Fault Handling.
  * Page Replacement Algorithms: FIFO, Optimal Page Replacement, LRU (Least Recently Used), LFU, MFU. Thrashing.
  * Disk Management: Disk Structure, Disk Scheduling Algorithms (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK, C-LOOK).
  * File System Interface: Access Methods, Directory Structures, Protection.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 2] Object Oriented Programming Using Java (BCAGN2C04T)
- Unit I: OOP Concepts & Java Fundamentals
  * Paradigm Shift: Object-Oriented vs Procedural Programming.
  * Core Principles: Encapsulation, Abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism.
  * Java Architecture: JVM (Java Virtual Machine), JRE, JDK, Bytecode, Garbage Collection.
  * Java Tokens, Identifiers, Keywords, Data Types, Variables, Type Conversion/Casting, Operators.
  * Control Flow: Conditionals, Loops, Command-Line Arguments.
- Unit II: Classes, Objects, Methods & Arrays
  * Class Declaration, Object Creation, Instance Variables, Method Syntax, Constructor Types (Default, Parameterized, Copy).
  * Keyword Usages: `this`, `static` (Variables, Methods, Blocks).
  * Method Overloading, Constructor Overloading, Object Reference Passing.
  * Arrays: 1D, 2D Arrays, Jagged Arrays.
  * String Manipulation: String class, StringBuffer, StringBuilder, String Methods, Wrapper Classes.
- Unit III: Inheritance, Interfaces & Polymorphism
  * Inheritance: Types (Single, Multilevel, Hierarchical), `super` keyword, Method Overriding, Dynamic Method Dispatch (Runtime Polymorphism).
  * Modifiers: `final` keyword (Variables, Methods, Classes), Access Modifiers (public, private, protected, default).
  * Abstract Classes & Abstract Methods.
  * Interfaces: Defining, Implementing, Extending Interfaces, Multiple Inheritance using Interfaces, Default/Static methods in Interfaces.
- Unit IV: Packages, Exception Handling, Multithreading & File I/O
  * Packages: Built-in packages (java.lang, java.util, java.io), User-defined package creation, Access Protection.
  * Exception Handling: Exception Hierarchy, Built-in Exceptions, `try`, `catch`, `finally`, `throw`, `throws`, Custom Exceptions.
  * Multithreading: Thread Class, Runnable Interface, Thread Lifecycle, Thread Priorities, Synchronization.
  * File I/O: Byte Streams vs Character Streams, Reading/Writing files using FileInputStream, FileOutputStream, FileReader, FileWriter.

  * Software Testing Fundamentals: Verification vs Validation, Test Cases Design.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS

[SUBJECT 4] Mathematical Foundation to Computer Science - II (BCAGN2E02T)
- Unit I: Mathematical Logic & Proof Techniques
  * Propositional Logic: Syntax, Semantics, Truth Tables, Tautologies, Contradictions, Logical Equivalence, Laws of Logic.
  * Rules of Inference, Modus Ponens, Modus Tollens. Normal Forms: Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF), Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF).
  * Predicate Logic: Predicates, Quantifiers (Universal, Existential), Nested Quantifiers.
  * Proof Methods: Direct Proof, Proof by Contraposition, Proof by Contradiction, Proof by Exhaustion, Mathematical Induction, Strong Induction.
- Unit II: Algebraic Structures
  * Binary Operations and Properties.
  * Groups: Definition, Axioms, Examples, Abelian Groups, Finite/Infinite Groups.
  * Subgroups, Cyclic Groups, Generators, Permutation Groups.
  * Cosets, Lagrange's Theorem and its Consequences.
  * Introduction to Rings, Integral Domains, and Fields.
- Unit III: Numerical Methods
  * Roots of Equations: Bisection Method, False Position (Regula-Falsi) Method, Newton-Raphson Method.
  * Interpolation: Forward and Backward Finite Differences, Newton's Forward/Backward Interpolation Formulas, Lagrange's Interpolation Formula.
  * Numerical Integration: Trapezoidal Rule, Simpson's 1/3 Rule, Simpson's 3/8 Rule.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 2] Cloud Computing & MLOps for Data Analysis
- Cloud Computing Foundations for Data Science:
  * Cloud Service Models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), Deployment Models (Public, Private, Hybrid).
  * Cloud Platforms: Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure overview.
  * Cloud Storage & Big Data Querying: AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Snowflake Data Cloud.
- Machine Learning Operations (MLOps):
  * MLOps Lifecycle: Data Versioning, Model Training, Model Testing, Model Deployment, Model Monitoring.
  * Version Control for ML: Git, Data Version Control (DVC).
  * Experiment Tracking & Model Registry: MLflow, Weights & Biases (W&B).
  * CI/CD Pipelines for Machine Learning: GitHub Actions, Automated Model Testing and Building.
  * Containerization & Orchestration: Docker Containers, Dockerfile creation, Container Images, Kubernetes Orchestration basics.

title: BCA DATASCIENCE SYLLABUS
content:
[SUBJECT 3] Data Security, Privacy & Ethics
- Data Privacy Laws & Regulations:
  * Global Privacy Frameworks: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).
  * Indian Privacy Legislation: Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act. Rights of Data Principals, Obligations of Data Fiduciaries.
- Privacy-Preserving Data Science:
  * Anonymization Techniques: Masking, Pseudonymization, K-Anonymity, L-Diversity, T-Closeness.
  * Differential Privacy: Mathematical Definition, Privacy Budget (Epsilon), Noise Addition Mechanisms (Laplace, Gaussian Mechanisms).
  * Federated Learning: Decentralized Model Training, Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning.
  * Secure Multiparty Computation (SMPC), Homomorphic Encryption basics.
- AI Ethics & Governance:
  * AI Governance Frameworks, Algorithmic Transparency, Explainable AI (XAI: SHAP, LIME).
  * Mitigating Algorithmic Bias, Fairness Metrics in Machine Learning, Responsible AI Principles.

content:
7.1 IDENTITY CARD REGULATIONS
* Identity cards must be worn visibly around the neck using a lanyard at all times while on campus.
* Mandatory for entry through campus gates, academic blocks, central library, and computer laboratories.
* Cards are strictly personal and non-transferable; lending an ID card results in fines or suspension.
* Lost cards must be reported immediately; duplicate cards are issued upon payment of a replacement fee (Rs. 100 - Rs. 500).
* A valid ID card is strictly compulsory for sitting in university examinations.

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
7.2 DRESS CODE GUIDELINES
* Male Students:
  - Permitted     : Formal shirts, formal trousers, neat and modest jeans, collared plain T-shirts,
                    formal/casual footwear, groomed hair; blazers and formal shoes on designated days.
  - Not Permitted : Round-neck/V-neck printed or slogan T-shirts, low-waist trousers, torn/distressed jeans,
                    unconventional hairstyles, or informal slippers.
* Female Students:
  - Permitted     : Salwar kameez/churidar, modest long kurtis, formal trousers/shirts, well-fitted plain jeans,
                    western formal wear, groomed hair; blazers on specified occasions.
  - Not Permitted : Crop tops, sleeveless tops, excessively tight-fitting outfits, revealing clothing,
                    skirts above knee length, torn jeans, or transparent clothing.

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
7.3 OPERATING TIMINGS
* Campus Working Hours      : 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM (Monday through Friday)
* Regular Class Schedules   : 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM / 4:00 PM
* Administrative Office     : 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM
* Central Library           : 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM (Monday - Friday); 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM (Saturday)
* Sports Complex Facilities : 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM (Monday - Saturday)
* Lunch Recess              : 11:40 AM to 12:10 PM

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
7.4 CAMPUS CODE OF CONDUCT
* Punctuality: Students must be seated in classrooms at the stroke of the bell. Late arrival may lead to denied entry.
* Decorum: Rise respectfully when faculty enter; eatables and open drinks are strictly prohibited inside classrooms,
  laboratories, and the library.
* Personal Conduct: Public displays of affection (PDA), fighting, abusive language, bullying, and theft are strictly banned.
* Mobile Phones: Phones must remain switched off inside classrooms, labs, and the library. Unauthorized use leads to confiscation.
* Prohibited Substances: Possession or consumption of alcohol, tobacco products, gutka, drugs, and intoxicants is strictly prohibited.
* Vehicle Parking: Parking is permitted only in designated bays (Rs. 1,000 for two-wheelers; Rs. 4,000 for four-wheelers).
  Helmets are compulsory for two-wheelers; maximum of one pillion rider allowed.

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
7.5 DISCIPLINARY FRAMEWORK: THE CARD SYSTEM
* Yellow Card (Serious Formal Warning):
  - Issued for: Classroom disruption, shouting/screaming, chewing gum/gutka, foul language, exam indiscipline,
    or disrespect toward staff. Serves as a penultimate opportunity to correct behaviour.
* Red Card (Final Warning / Last Opportunity):
  - Issued for: Accumulating two Yellow Cards, aggressive/violent behaviour, humiliation of faculty/staff,
    examination cheating, contacting media/outsiders without authorization, or damaging the university's reputation.
  - May lead to suspension, semester debarment, or dismissal.
* Green Card (Recognition of Excellence):
  - Awarded for: Exemplary moral integrity, academic distinction, active community service, kindness,
    and inspiring peer leadership.

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
7.6 ANTI-RAGGING REGULATIONS
* Strict Zero-Tolerance: Ragging in any form (verbal, physical, sexual, or psychological) is a criminal offence.
* Consequences: Immediate dismissal, FIR lodging under Government of India guidelines, and academic blacklisting.
* Mandatory Compliance: Students and parents must submit annual anti-ragging affidavits online via:
  www.antiragging.in or www.c4yindia.org.
* Reporting: Contact the Anti-Ragging Committee via email at: antiragging@xup.ac.in.

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
8.1 DEGREE STRUCTURE (NEP 2020 COMPLIANT)
* Multi-Exit & Entry Framework:
  - Year 1 Completion (Min 40-44 credits) -> Undergraduate Certificate
  - Year 2 Completion (Min 80-88 credits) -> Undergraduate Diploma
  - Year 3 Completion (Min 120-132 credits) -> Bachelor's Degree
  - Year 4 Completion (Min 160-176 credits) -> Bachelor's Degree with Honours / Honours with Research
* Credit Equivalents:
  - 1 Credit (Theory/Lecture/Tutorial) = 15 Hours of classroom engagement.
  - 1 Credit (Practical/Lab/Internship/Community Fieldwork) = 30 Hours of practical engagement.
* Academic Bank of Credits (ABC):
  - All students are registered with the National ABC portal for seamless digital credit accumulation and redemption.

title: HANDBOOK3
content:
8.2 CLASSROOM ATTENDANCE & LEAVE POLICY

title: ST XAVIERS CAMPUS RULES
content:
1. CODE OF CONDUCT & DISCIPLINE:
• Identity Cards: Carrying and displaying the official college Identity Card is mandatory at all times inside the campus, library, laboratories, and examination halls. Security staff may deny entry without a valid ID.
• Discipline: Students must maintain decorum, mutual respect, and proper behavior with faculty members, non-teaching staff, and fellow students.
• Prohibition of Ragging: Ragging in any form is strictly banned as per UGC guidelines and supreme court directives. Any student found guilty of ragging will face immediate expulsion and legal action.
• Substance Banned: Smoking, consumption of alcohol, tobacco, or drugs inside the college premises is strictly prohibited and punishable with severe disciplinary action or rustication.
• Use of Mobile Phones: Mobile phones must be kept on silent mode during lectures, practical labs, library hours, and official college functions. Unapproved recording or photography is strictly forbidden.

title: ST XAVIERS CAMPUS RULES
content:
1. ATTENDANCE & LEAVE POLICY:
• Mandatory Attendance: Minimum 75% attendance in theory lectures, tutorials, and practical classes is compulsory to be eligible to sit for semester examinations.
• Shortage of Attendance: Students failing to meet the minimum attendance requirement will not be allowed to appear in the end-semester university examinations.
• Leave Sanction: Leaves exceeding 3 days require a written application along with supporting documents (e.g., Medical Certificate for medical leave) submitted to the Principal/HOD for formal approval.

title: ST XAVIERS CAMPUS RULES
content:

• College Dress Code: Students are required to follow the prescribed college dress code/uniform on specified days and official events.
• Decent Attire: On non-uniform days, students must wear modest and decent casual clothes suitable for an educational institution. Shorts, sleeveless clothing, or inappropriate print wear are not permitted.

title: ST XAVIERS CAMPUS RULES
content:

• Library Cards: Books will only be issued upon presenting a valid Library/ID Card.
• Silence Maintenance: Strict silence must be observed inside the central library and reading room areas.
• Book Return & Fines: Books must be returned or renewed on or before the due date. A fine will be charged per day for overdue books as per library norms.
• Book Damage/Loss: Damaged or lost books must be replaced with a new copy or paid for as per library evaluation rules.

title: ST XAVIERS CAMPUS RULES
content:

• Preservation of Property: Students must handle college property, lab computers, library books, furniture, and equipment with extreme care. Any intentional damage to college property will result in heavy financial penalties and disciplinary action.
• Cleanliness: Littering is strictly forbidden. Students must dispose of waste in designated dustbins placed across campus.
• Parking: Two-wheelers and bicycles must be parked neatly in the designated student parking area only.

title: Lost ID Card
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: Don't panic! The quickest practical route is to visit the Student Affairs Helpdesk in Admin Block A, Room 104 between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM. First, ask the front desk officer for an emergency Temporary Gate Slip so campus security won't stop you at the gates or library. Then pay the fee at Cashier Window 2—card payment is much faster than cash. Pro-tip from seniors: Keep a clear photo of your ID card barcode on your phone; security and the library scanner will often accept that for the day!
Question: I lost my university ID card. What should I do?

title: Document Verification Venue & Queue
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: While the official venue is the Multi-Purpose Hall in Wing C, the line gets super long by 10:00 AM. Seniors strongly advise reaching by 8:15 AM to collect a token number from Counter 1. The document verification desks are arranged alphabetically by department (A-F, G-M, N-Z), so check the big whiteboards at the hall entrance before standing in the general line.
Question: Where do students usually go for document verification?

title: Document Verification Preparation
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: Bring at least 4 passport-size photographs and 3 extra photocopies of every certificate in a clean transparent folder. Crucial tip: Bring your own blue ink pen, stapler, and glue stick! The stationery stall inside the campus is a 10-minute walk away across the grounds and usually has a massive queue on verification days.
Question: What should I carry for document verification?

title: Missed Deadlines & Registration Overrides
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: Avoid sending an email to the general university helpdesk email because they take 3 to 5 business days to reply during registration week. Instead, go straight in person to your Department Secretary or your designated Faculty Advisor at 9:30 AM with a handwritten, signed request letter explaining your reason. They have administrative override access and can sign Form AC-10 on the spot.
Question: I missed a deadline. Who should I contact?

title: Hostel Allocation & Move-In
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: Room keys are handed out by the Ground Floor Caretaker in each residence block. The fastest move-in is between 11:00 AM and 2:00 PM when lines thin out. Tip from seniors: If you have an option, ask for a 2nd or 3rd floor room (ground floor gets noisy near the entry lobby). Bring a 3-pin extension cord and a mattress topper because room outlets are often far from the study desk.
Question: How do I get my hostel allocation?

title: Campus Entry without ID
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: If your physical ID isn't issued yet (freshers or lost cards), show your digital Provisional Admission Letter or fee receipt on your smartphone along with any government ID (driver's license or passport) at Main Gate 2. The security team maintains a Visitor Entry Register and will let you in immediately without any hassle.
Question: What happens if I don't have my ID card yet?

title: Submitting Documents & Forms
source: Student Community Reports — Campus Experience Network
content:
Experience: For immediate peace of mind, do not use the physical drop-box outside the admissions office (it gets cleared only once every 48 hours). Instead, hand your documents directly to the desk officer at Window 3 (Student Affairs) and ask them to stamp your duplicate copy with an official 'Received' date stamp as your proof of submission.
